title: Quiet time - add ability to automatically mute all/some devices according to times or events
line: Sound settings now have quiet hours that mute all audio between two times, and again on login or wake-up if it was unmuted in between.
explanation: Plasma had no way to keep the computer silent at set times, so a laptop opened or woken at night or at work could play sounds before the user had a chance to mute it. The change adds a 'Quiet hours: Mute all audio from <time> to <time>' option to the Sound settings' Volume Controls page. The audio kded module checks it every minute and on config changes, and turns on the existing global mute when quiet hours begin, on login and on every wake-up from suspend during quiet hours; when they end it turns the mute back off (without the feedback sound) only if quiet hours had turned it on and the user didn't change it meanwhile.

commits.message:
kded: add quiet hours that mute all audio at set times

There was no way to keep the computer silent at night or at work, so it
could make noise on login or wake-up before audio could be muted. Quiet
hours now mute all audio between two times, on login and on wake-up.

BUG: 429663

media.caption: Master: Sound > Configure Volume Controls has no way to schedule muting
Patched: new 'Quiet hours: Mute all audio from … to …' option; enabled with a range that includes the current time, audio mutes at once (muted icon in the tray)
When quiet hours end (6:31 PM here) the audio is unmuted again by itself
Audio unmuted by hand during quiet hours, then the system suspends and wakes up: it is muted again
